That is a result about 1.3, which is the aggressive end.  Wave 35 prices the MILD end and the other mechanism the phrase 'token penalties' actually covers.

grid.note: this row IS the sealed decode; it is in the table because a grid without its own null is a grid of unanchored numbers

headline: TWENTY child-settings, 300 lanes, ZERO hand-confirmed recoveries, and every setting is net-negative.  The dose-response on the damage side is monotone and complete -- penalty 1.1 costs 3 of the 13 signal lanes, 1.15 costs 7, 1.3 costs all 13 -- and the recovery side is flat at zero the whole way down.  There is no mild setting that buys anything.
the_mechanistic_finding: THE PENALTY MANUFACTURES READABILITY; IT DOES NOT UNBLOCK CONTENT.  Every arm with a penalty in it makes 37 of 37 artifact lanes readable.  The HARD n-gram ban alone leaves SIX of them still unreadable -- exactly the six the sealed decode also fails to make readable -- because a model can loop with a period longer than three tokens and the ban cannot touch that.  So the multiplicative penalty's headline effect is an artifact of forcing novel tokens into the argmax, not of removing something that was suppressing an answer.  That is the clearest evidence in either wave that there is nothing waiting behind the loop.
the_cheapest_arm_and_why_it_still_does_n: no-repeat-ngram 3 with no penalty is the least damaging arm in the grid (3 of 13 signal lanes lost, tied with penalty 1.1) and it is the one with the strongest prior reason to work: it removes a repeating token from the argmax entirely and leaves every other token at EXACTLY its sealed logit, so a lane that was answering cannot be flattened by rescaling.  It recovers nothing anyway.

the_nearest_miss_in_the_whole_grid.text: The question is based on the following instructions. The question is asked regarding the availability of the tool. The North gate has been provided this month. What is the tool checkout for you? If the note doesn't answer something.
the_nearest_miss_in_the_whole_grid.verdict: REJECTED, and recorded verbatim because it is the closest anything came.  The lane asks which day is allowed, what the latest checkout time is, and which gate to avoid.  This surfaces the token North -- which the sealed decode of this child does not -- but it says the gate has been PROVIDED rather than closed, gives no day and no time, and inverts into a question back at the asker.  A correct token is not an answer.

the_direction_this_could_have_gone: The pre-registration recorded, before any run, that if any setting recovered a real answer without killing the signal lanes the artifact clause's remedy would be cheaper than wave 34 priced it and this file would say so.  It does not say so.
what_this_does_and_does_not_refute: It does NOT refute the canonical standard.  A lane that produces no readable text is still no evidence about intelligence in either direction, and that is the standard's actual claim.  What it refutes, now across six settings and two mechanisms rather than one value of one knob, is the REMEDY attached to it: on this population, at inference time, there is nothing waiting behind the loop.  Retraining is the untested half of the clause and it is a stage-2 activity under the staged escalation policy, so it may not be prototyped while stage 1 is open.
